gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-savate: Savate keeps its curves wide open and its lines clean. Under Plakkaat's heavy, nearly closed letters, a paragraph of this sans-serif body feels like stepping out into daylight.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-stack-sans-headli: Approachable and crisp, Stack Sans Headline lays down a monoline body with generous gaps beneath Plakkaat's heavy, bent-straw capitals. Weight above, openness below.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-manrope: Heavy and blunt, Plakkaat looks bent from straw, while Manrope's bright, open curves hold a single steady line beneath it. One hits hard; the other keeps going.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-space-grotesk: Chunky, tightly curled headline letters sit over Space Grotesk, whose lowercase is moderate in height, with hollow counters that breathe. Reading it feels light after Plakkaat.
gen-dafont-pricedown-archivo: Archivo reads big and open, its curves flaring outward with a commanding x-height. Pricedown's glass-bulb lowercase bowls up top make the sans-serif body feel even more spacious, so size it up generously for comfort.
gen-dafont-pricedown-fs-paquito: Confident from the first line, Pricedown blows up its lowercase bowls like glass bulbs and leaves only a slit for apertures. And Paquito, a text serif with almost no gap between x-height and caps, stays comfortable in small doses.
gen-dafont-pricedown-fs-ranade: Playful but grounded, Pricedown gets its bulb-shaped lowercase noticed fast. Ranade's sans-serif body, with only slight weight shifts and stroke ends set far apart, gives all that closed roundness an open, spread-out partner.
gen-dafont-pricedown-poppins: Playful and classic, Pricedown fills its tall lowercase with glassy bowls and pen-nib slits for apertures. And Poppins, a sans-serif with loose curves and no thick-thin flicker, lets that personality sit quietly above it.
gen-dafont-prime-fs-alpino: Chunky yet friendly, Prime hangs its bulky lowercase like clothespins on a line, with softly shifting strokes. And Alpino, a plain sans with tall bodies, stingy spacing and curve endings kept apart, settles in beneath it casually.
gen-dafont-prime-fs-asap: Prime brings softly varied strokes and bulky lowercase proportions. Asap sits below as a sans-serif with open arcs and lowercase nearly as tall as its capitals, so the clear difference is closed heading shapes against open body ones.
